Tail index of a heavy-tailed count

Source: R/cconc.R
hilltl.Rd

The exponent alpha of a power-law tail, P(X = k) proportional to k^-alpha above a threshold xmin, as when a few people account for most repeat placements or most steps of an offender's path are short and a few very long (Clauset, Shalizi and Newman 2009). For counts the maximum likelihood estimate of the discrete law is the default, its normalising constant the Hurwitz zeta function zeta(alpha, xmin); approx = TRUE gives the closed form with xmin - 1/2, and discrete = FALSE the continuous Hill estimator 1 + n / sum log(x / xmin) for measurements such as distances. ks is the Kolmogorov-Smirnov distance between the tail and the fitted law: an exponent is only as good as that fit. The values at or below 0 are left out.

Usage

hilltl(x, xmin = NULL, discrete = TRUE, approx = FALSE, mintl = 3)

Arguments

x

The values: numbers from 0.

xmin

NULL (the 50th largest value, or the smallest when there are fewer than 50) or the threshold: one positive number.

discrete

TRUE for counts, FALSE for measurements.

approx

TRUE for the closed form for counts instead of the maximum likelihood estimate.

mintl

The fewest tail values to fit to: a whole number (at least 2 are always needed).

Value

An object of class hilltl, a list: alpha and its standard error se (the observed information for the discrete estimate, (alpha - 1) / sqrt(n) otherwise; both NA when no fit is made), xmin, ntl (the tail size), ks, reliable (TRUE with 50 or more tail values and an estimate inside the search interval [1.0001, 25]) and method.

References

Clauset, A., Shalizi, C. R. and Newman, M. E. J. (2009). Power-law distributions in empirical data. SIAM Review, 51(4), 661-703. doi:10.1137/070710111

Hill, B. M. (1975). A simple general approach to inference about the tail of a distribution. The Annals of Statistics, 3(5), 1163-1174. doi:10.1214/aos/1176343247

Examples

set.seed(4)
k <- floor(runif(400)^(-1 / 1.5))
hilltl(k, xmin = 1)
#> hilltl: discrete maximum likelihood
#> alpha 2.146 (se 0.0619), xmin 1, 400 tail values, KS 0.0377
